paper_metadata.title: Credit Default Prediction with Projected Quantum Feature Models and Ensembles

summary: The paper evaluates projected quantum feature (PQF) models with a Heisenberg feature map for credit-default prediction using up to 101 qubits and circuits with ~870 two‑qubit gates. Standalone quantum models achieve slightly lower accuracy than classical XGBoost (e.g., 88.9% vs 89.8% on hardware), but hybrid ensembles combining classical and quantum predictions improve the CDR metric by about 0.0009–0.0041 over classical baselines on a 10,000‑sample dataset.

experiments.description: Projected quantum feature map (Heisenberg feature map) with XGBoost classifier evaluated on balanced credit-default subsamples using classical simulation backends.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are scaled to [0.3, 0.8], shuffled, then encoded into a Heisenberg feature map circuit; expectation values of local observables are projected back to classical features for XGBoost.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of credit default; optimize predictive performance on default prediction dataset using CDR/accuracy/AUC depending on split.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Heisenberg-model-inspired feature map with pairwise XX+YY+ZZ interactions

problem_instance.description: Credit card default prediction on a public benchmark dataset from the American Express default prediction competition.

dataset_specification.description: Public Kaggle competition dataset; balanced subsamples used for simulator/hardware experiments; one-month reduced dataset used for classical benchmark; unbalanced 10,000-sample subset used for ensemble evaluation.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Removed non-modeling variables and zero-variance features; class-balanced or stratified subsampling; train/test split 50/50 for benchmark and balanced studies; features scaled with MinMaxScaler to [0.3, 0.8]; feature order randomized with ShuffleFeatures; feature importance selected with Random Forest for some trials; unbalanced subset maintained ~80% negatives and 20% positives.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 5-fold cross-validation; test-set evaluation; Bayesian optimization with 15 random seeds for ensemble study; repeated runs across multiple qubit counts and backends.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Qiskit preset pass manager optimization level 3; native basis gates after transpilation
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: MinMax scaling to [0.3, 0.8]; ShuffleFeatures; Random Forest feature selection in some trials
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Expectation values from projected quantum features fed into XGBoost; ensemble probabilities combined by averaging or logistic regression in later experiments

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or runtime speedup claim is made; only empirical benchmarking of predictive performance is reported.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; simulations up to 101 qubits using statevector/MPS but no scaling analysis demonstrating quantum speedup.
limiting_factors: Classical XGBoost baseline achieves higher accuracy (e.g., 89.1% vs 86.4% in statevector experiment)
Quantum component only used as feature transformer
Evaluation performed on small balanced subsets (~1,000 samples)
